My dear Levushka,

I am at present stationed at Hull and am taking the
opportunity to pen you a few lines.

First of all, I write in the name of Valentin and
request you and Lodn not to write any more temporary in his
name, because he is very much afraid that he will be subjected
to repressive measures for removing. He is already registered
as having removed and this is causing him a lot of unpleasant-
ness in his work and, at the present moment, he is expecting
other complications. All this, of course, for you is incom-
prehensible, but such are our conditions of life.

As for me, I write you only when I am abroad and, for
that reason, in all the numerous forms that have to be filled
in, I am disowning all contact with you. I think this will
not be discovered, although our agency - that is - Soviet -
penetrates everywhere.

In general, I am living in the old way, that is to
say, I am sailing and am in L - on now and then.

I do not know if I will continue long there because
my health becomes worse and worse and circumstances do not
permit being treated or even taking a rest. They give no leave
and nothing can be done in the few days we are in L - on, in
this respect, to say nothing of being in a complete state of
going out of one's mind. In general, a lunatic asylum.

Demands are increasing daily and concurrently with
them every punitive (illegible).

It is impossible to fulfill all this.

Now matters have gone so far that they are demanding
precise railway punctuality and are not admitting storms or
fogs, in fact - nothing.- Subsequently, I have fears that they
will stop altogether paying the 18% in bills on Torgsin and will

1935年11月13日。

亲爱的 Levushka：

我目前驻守在赫尔（Hull），借此机会给你写几行字。

首先，我以瓦伦丁（Valentin）的名义写信，请求你和 Lodn 不要再以他的名义写任何关于搬迁的临时信件，因为他非常害怕会因搬迁而受到压制性措施。他已经被登记为已搬迁，这给他的工作带来了许多不愉快，而且目前他正担心会出现其他复杂情况。当然，这一切对你们来说是不可理解的，但这就是我们的生活状况。

至于我，只有当我在国外时才给你写信，因此，在所有必须填写的众多表格中，我都否认与你有过任何联系。我想这不会被发现，尽管我们的机构——即苏联——渗透到了各个地方。

总的来说，我还是过着老样子，也就是说，我在航行，偶尔会在 L - on。

我不知道我是否能在那里待很久，因为我的健康状况越来越差，而且环境不允许接受治疗，甚至不允许休息。他们不给假期，我们在 L - on 的那几天里，在这方面什么都做不了，更不用说处于完全精神崩溃的状态了。总之，就像疯人院一样。

March 4, 1936
Shanghai,
China.

Sir,

We are very indignant when we learn of the criminal
acts of Japanese imperialism now occurring in China, which
have induced us to found the World League against Conquest
and Colonisation, with the object of conducting an energetic
campaign throughout the whole world in opposition to
Nippon barbarism which means to reduce the millenial
civilisation of China to the humiliating level of Colonies.

You know that for the past few years Japan has been
detested by America and the European Powers. Therefore it
is not unseasonable to force by means of popular pressure
England, The United States, Germany, Russia and France to
react against your aggressor by useful collective action.

Now to succeed in such a grandiose scheme as this
we naturally need adherents in all countries, especially
in China. To this end we forward you herewith membership
forms and request that you will be so good as to return
them to us after filling them in. We shall be glad to have
you join our World League so that you may collaborate with
us in saving the honour and independence of your country.

Hoping to hear from you shortly,

Yours sincerely ...........

1936年3月4日
中国，上海。

先生：

当我们得知日本帝国主义目前在中国发生的罪行时，我们感到极为愤慨，这些罪行促使我们成立了“世界反征服与反殖民联盟”，旨在在全世界范围内开展一场有力的运动，反对日本野蛮行径，这种行径意在将中国千年的文明降低到殖民地的屈辱水平。

您知道，在过去几年里，日本一直受到美国和欧洲列强的憎恶。因此，通过民众压力迫使英国、美国、德国、俄国和法国采取有用的集体行动来对抗您的侵略者，并非不合时宜。

现在，要成功实施如此宏大的计划，我们自然需要各国的支持者，尤其是中国的支持者。为此，我们随函附上会员申请表，恳请您填好后退还给我们。我们将很高兴您加入我们的世界联盟，以便您与我们合作，拯救贵国的荣誉和独立。

盼早日复音，

此致

Translation of an extract from an article entitled "Railways in
China" published in the "Min Chung Chow Pao" (民衆周報), Vol. 3,
Issue 4 :-

The British, French, German and Japanese robbers loudly
advocated equal enjoyment of privileges;
They all wanted to seize control of railroads.
France intended to occupy our territory in the South-west,
And built the Yunnan-Annam Railway.
French soldiers were stationed along the line;
It was very dangerous.
Britain was as bad.
She built a railway in Kowloon,
By which she took control of the south gate of China.
The economic invasion was deplorable.
British troops were stationed in Hongkong.
If anything happened, they could come immediately by the
railway and commit violent acts.
Germany forcibly occupied Kiaochow and Tsingtao,
and constructed a railway from Tsinan to Lutung,
The wealth of Shantung was thus seized by her.
Japan was fighting against Russia.
She built the Antung-Fengtien Railway, connecting Chosen
with Liaoning.
She used the railway to transport soldiers.
She was so ambitious that she acted insanely.
After the Russo-Japanese war, the South Manchurian Railway
came under control of Japan.
Using the railways as bases, Japan decided upon a
"continental policy" to invade Manchuria and Mongolia.
The above-mentioned railways are like blood-sucking leeches.
The people were deprived of all their wealth.
The Powers set up a net of invasion and clearly demarcated
their spheres of influence.
Our territory will become that of others.
Is this not painful?

Further to attached file, the reason the matter was
referred to the M.A. for advice was because of the fact that
Article 7 of the Press Law provides only for punishment of the
publisher for non-registration.
While there is good reason to believe that the magazine
in question is being printed at 390 Wuchow Road, and sold at
278 Foochow Road, a printed notice on the cover of the magazine
states that it is published by the Common Reading Matter
Compilation Society (通俗讀物編刊社), c/o Yenching University,
Peiping, which also requested that all contributions to the
magazine be forwarded to that address. The M.A. while
examining the question noticed that the contents of the
magazine contained matter which is anti-foreign as well as
anti-Japanese, and suggested that as there was difficulty in
defining whether the publisher should be considered the
printer in Shanghai or the Society in Peiping, a charge should
be brought against the printer and distributor in Shanghai under
Article 153, Section 2, of Chinese Criminal Code and a further
charge under Article 7 of the Press Law, stating that in his
opinion the matter contained in the magazine constituted a
clear case contravening the order of the National Government,
dated 10/6/35, which is covered by Article 153 of C.C.C.

Mr. Tsang : The accused is charged under Article 153(2) of the C.C.C. and further charged under Art. 7 of the Press Law. Q. Was the 'Min Chung Chow Pao' sold by you store ?.

June 5, 1937.
Lih Pao:
APPEAL TO BE LODGED AGAINST FINE FOR NON-REGISTRATION
OF MAGAZINE
On May 18, over 10,000 copies of the "Min Chung
Chow Pao" (民衆周報), a weekly magazine, published by
the Common Reading Matter Compilation Society (通俗讀物編刊社)
in Peiping, were seized by the Municipal Police at the Kai
Ming Bookstore (開明書店), which is the sales office of
the magazine in question, and Tsang Sih-sung (章錫琛),
Manager of the store, was proceeded against at the Shanghai
First Special District Court under Article 153, Section 2,
of the Chinese Criminal Code and Article 7 of the Chinese
Press Law for selling the magazine which is alleged to be
anti-Japanese in nature and is not registered with the
competent authorities concerned.
On the morning of June 4, the Court fined
Tsang Sih-sung $30 for non-registration and dismissed the
charge for contravening the order of the National Government
under Article 153, Section 2, of the Chinese Criminal
Code. The Court also directed that pending registration,
the magazine should suspend publication.
According to information given by a responsible
employee of the Kai Ming Bookstore, Li Ih-fei (李飛)
is the publisher of the magazine in question.
There is no reason for Tsang Sih-sung to
undertake responsibility for the question of registration.
Moreover, an application for registration was submitted
when the magazine was published in Peiping and another
application was forwarded to the local Tangpu Headquarters
and Government organs when the Sales office was removed to
Shanghai.
Furthermore, Article 7 of the Chinese Press
Law stipulates that application for registration should
be submitted 15 days before the commencing of publication,
but there is no ruling in the Law that the publication of
those newspapers and magazines which have already submitted
applications for registration should be prohibited before
certificates of registration have been issued.
For this reason, Tsang Sih-sung has decided
to lodge an appeal at the Second Branch of the Kiangsu
High Court.

May 21, 1937. Morning Translation.

Lih Pao :-
SEIZURE OF "MIN CHUNG CHOW PAO" : CONTAINS GENERAL FENG
YU-HSIANG'S POEMS

The case regarding the seizure of the "Min
Chung Chow Pao" ( 民衆週報 ), published by the Common
Reading Matter Compilation Society ( 通俗讀物編刊社 ), Peiping,
came up before the Shanghai First Special District Court
on May 19. The Municipal Police gave as its reason for
prosecution the fact that the seized magazine constituted
a menace to peace and order, incited others to commit crimes
and violated the Press Law.
On May 20, a responsible member of the Kai
Ming Bookstore ( 開明書店 ) made the following statement
to our reporter :- "Before the publication of the 'Min
Chung Chow Pao', an application was submitted to the
Ministry of Interior for registration. The magazine
has been published in Shanghai from Volume Two, Issue No.4.
The management of the bookstore has presented the magazine
to the Shanghai City Government for examination, and also
requested the local Tangpu Headquarters to apply to the
Central Propaganda Department for registration. Although
the registration certificate has not yet been secured,
the publication is not fundamentally contrary to the
Press Law".
It is reported that the Settlement authorities
are the movers of the seizure of the "Min Chung Chow Pao"
and the search warrants were applied for by the Municipal
Police to the Court.
On May 20, our reporter collected several
copies of the "Min Chung Chow Pao" in an endeavour to
find out why the magazine was seized. A perusal shows
that it is an ordinary magazine. Besides containing
articles by the editors and cartoons, the magazine frequently
publishes the writings of General Feng Yu-hsiang, Vice-
Chairman of the Military Affairs Commission. For instance,
in its Volume 3, Issue No. 7, the magazine contains a
poem written by General Feng concerning soldiers in farming
districts. The following is part of this poem :-
"The four sides of the farming villages are silent.
"The sound of running water is heard in the room.
"Being unable to sleep, we sit up at mid-night,
"Pondering over our brethren who are being slaughtered.
"The four provinces have been stolen from us,
"The 3,000,000 rifles are taken over by the enemy.
"If we do not take the chance to-day to save the nation,
"We will soon see our race annihilated".
General Feng's poem written while living in
the country is contained in Volume 3, Issue No. 5 of this
magazine and many of his articles are published in other
issues. It is believed that General Feng's writings
do not violate the law.
The present editor of the magazine is Mr.Koo
Chih-kong ( 顧志公 ) who is a graduate of the Peiping
University and now a professor there. It is known that
he is not a "radical element". The reason for the seizure
of the "Min Chung Chow Pao" is still doubtful.
No information has come from the North after
the seizure of the magazine and it is not known whether
the magazine will be similarly seized in the North. The
Manager of the Kai Ming Bookstore has notified the Common
Reading Matter Compilation Society of the case.

《立报》：
查封《民众周报》：内含冯玉祥将军诗作

关于查封由北平通俗读物编刊社出版的《民众周报》一案，于5月19日在上海第一特区地方法院开庭审理。工部局警务处提出的起诉理由是，被查封的杂志构成对和平与秩序的威胁，煽动他人犯罪，并违反《出版法》。
5月20日，开明书店的一位负责人向记者发表如下声明：“在《民众周报》出版前，已向内政部提交注册申请。该杂志自第二卷第四期起在上海出版。书店管理层已将杂志呈送上海市政府审查，并请求当地汤浦总部向中央宣传部申请注册。虽然尚未取得注册证，但该出版物并不根本违背《出版法》。”
据悉，租界当局是查封《民众周报》的发起者，搜查令由工部局警务处向法院申请。
5月20日，本报记者收集了几份《民众周报》，试图查明杂志被查禁的原因。浏览显示，这是一份普通杂志。除了刊登编辑文章和漫画外，该杂志经常刊登军事委员会副委员长冯玉祥将军的文章。例如，在其第三卷第七期中，刊登了冯将军所作的一首关于农村士兵的诗。以下是这首诗的部分内容：
“农村四周静悄悄。
“屋内听得流水声。
“夜半难眠坐起身，
“思念同胞遭屠戮。
“四省国土被窃去，

May 21, 1937. Morning Translation.

Lih Pao :-

SEIZURE OF "MIN CHUNG CHOW PAO" : CONTAINS GENERAL FENG
YU-HSIANG'S POEMS

The case regarding the seizure of the "Min
Chung Chow Pao" ( 民衆週刊 ), published by the Common
Reading Matter Compilation Society ( 通俗讀物編刊社 ), Peiping,
came up before the Shanghai First Special District Court
on May 19. The Municipal Police gave as its reason for
prosecution the fact that the seized magazine constituted
a menace to peace and order, incited others to commit crimes
and violated the Press Law.
On May 20, a responsible member of the Kai
Ming Bookstore ( 開明書店 ) made the following statement
to our reporter :- "Before the publication of the 'Min
Chung Chow Pao', an application was submitted to the
Ministry of Interior for registration. The magazine
has been published in Shanghai from Volume Two, Issue No.4.
The management of the bookstore has presented the magazine
to the Shanghai City Government for examination, and also
requested the local Tangpu Headquarters to apply to the
Central Propaganda Department for registration. Although
the registration certificate has not yet been secured,
the publication is not fundamentally contrary to the
Press Law".
It is reported that the Settlement authorities
are the movers of the seizure of the "Min Chung Chow Pao"
and the search warrants were applied for by the Municipal
Police to the Court.
On May 20, our reporter collected several
copies of the "Min Chung Chow Pao" in an endeavour to
find out why the magazine was seized. A perusal shows
that it is an ordinary magazine. Besides containing
articles by the editors and cartoons, the magazine frequently
publishes the writings of General Feng Yu-hsiang, Vice-
Chairman of the Military Affairs Commission. For instance,
in its Volume 3, Issue No. 7, the magazine contains a
poem written by General Feng concerning soldiers in farming
districts. The following is part of this poem :-
"The four sides of the farming villages are silent.
"The sound of running water is heard in the room.
"Being unable to sleep, we sit up at mid-night,
"Pondering over our brethren who are being slaughtered.
"The four provinces have been stolen from us,
"The 3,000,000 rifles are taken over by the enemy.
"If we do not take the chance to-day to save the nation,
"We will soon see our race annihilated".
General Feng's poem written while living in
the country is contained in Volume 3, Issue No. 5 of this
magazine and many of his articles are published in other
issues. It is believed that General Feng's writings
do not violate the law.
The present editor of the magazine is Mr.Koo
Chih-kong ( 顧質剛 ) who is a graduate of the Peiping
University and now a professor there. It is known that
he is not a "radical element". The reason for the seizure
of the "Min Chung Chow Pao" is still doubtful.
No information has come from the North after
the seizure of the magazine and it is not known whether
the magazine will be similarly seized in the North. The
Manager of the Kai Ming Bookstore has notified the Common
Reading Matter Compilation Society of the case.

《立报》：
查封《民众周刊》：内含冯玉祥将军诗作

关于查封由北平通俗读物编刊社出版的《民众周刊》一案，于5月19日在上海第一特区地方法院开庭审理。工部局警务处提出的起诉理由是，被查封的杂志构成对和平与秩序的威胁，煽动他人犯罪，并违反《出版法》。
5月20日，开明书店的一位负责人向记者发表如下声明：“在《民众周刊》出版前，已向内政部提交注册申请。该杂志自第二卷第四期起在上海出版。书店管理层已将杂志呈送上海市政府审查，并请求当地汤浦总部向中央宣传部申请注册。虽然尚未取得注册证，但该出版物并不根本违背《出版法》。”
据悉，租界当局是查封《民众周刊》的发起者，搜查令由工部局警务处向法院申请。

“民族灭亡在眼前。”

Lih Pao published the following report on May 19, 1937.

COPIES OF MAGAZINE SEIZED BY POLICE

The Kai Ming Bookstore (開明書店), Foochow Road,
was searched by Chinese and foreign detectives of the Central
Police Station at about 4 p.m. May 18, when more than 10,000
copies of a weekly magazine entitled "Ming Chung Cheu Pao"
(民衆周報 "People's Weekly"), which is edited and published
by the Common Reading Matter Compilation Society (通俗讀物編刊社,
Peiping, were taken to the Station. Searches were also
carried out in bookstores and magazine companies along Foochow
Road, and copies of the magazine in question seized in these
premises were all removed to the Station.

It is said that the searches were executed on the
order of the Court owing to the fact that the magazine had
repeatedly published articles endangering friendly relations
with foreign Powers.

The "Ming Chung Cheu Pao" ("People's Weekly") is
published by one Li Ih-fei (李一非). Formerly, the
magazine was edited by one Hsu Ping-chong (徐炳), but
recently, the editorship has been undertaken by one Koo Chih-
kong (顧頡剛), a professor of the Peiping University.
The magazine contains mostly common reading matter and the
major number of its readers are middle school students.
The latest issue is Volume III, No.9.

The "Ming Chung Cheu Pao" was formerly printed in
Peiping, but in order to secure an extensive sale of the
magazine, the printing has been taken over by the Kai Ming
Bookstore since Volume II, Issue No.4. About 7,000 copies
were circulated in Peiping, but the circulation in Shanghai is
poor.

《立报》于1937年5月19日刊登了以下报道。

警方查获杂志副本

5月18日下午4时许，中央捕房的中外籍侦探搜查了福州路的开明书店，查获由北平通俗读物编刊社编辑出版的周刊《民众周报》（英文名拼写为 "Ming Chung Cheu Pao"）一万多册，并押送至捕房。福州路沿线的书店和杂志公司也进行了搜查，在这些场所查获的该杂志副本均被移送至捕房。

据悉，此次搜查是奉法院命令执行，原因是该杂志多次刊登危害与外国列强友好关系的文章。

《民众周报》由李一非出版。此前，该杂志由徐炳编辑，但最近编辑工作已由北京大学教授顾颉刚（Koo Chih-kong）接手。该杂志内容多为通俗读物，读者大多为中学生。最新一期为第三卷第九期。

《民众周报》原在北平印刷，但为了扩大销量，自第二卷第四期起由开明书店承接印刷。该杂志在北平的发行量约为7,000份，但在上海的销路不佳。
